# Derivation 3.3B — Rejected null-probe source route {#sec-derivation-03-03B-null-probe-diagnostic .unnumbered}

## Purpose

This appendix records why a natural quadratic null-probe reading is not the
carrier source map used by Chapter 3.

## Role, regime, and status

- **Role:** structural diagnostic.
- **Regime:** weak stationary comparison.
- **Status:** rejected as a source identification.
- **Non-claim:** the rejection does not depend on a closed frame-drag action or
  on the formerly advertised $\kappa_A=4$ derivation chain.

## Quadratic null contractions

For $l_k^\pm=(1,\pm e_k)$, a classical stress tensor gives

$$
T_{\mu\nu}l_k^{\pm\mu}l_k^{\pm\nu}
=T_{00}\pm2T_{0k}+T_{kk}.
$$

If one identified the source channels with these contractions,

$$
\mathcal J_k^\pm\stackrel{?}{=}
\lambda T_{\mu\nu}l_k^{\pm\mu}l_k^{\pm\nu},
$$

then

$$
\mathcal M_k=\lambda(T_{00}+T_{kk}),
\qquad
\mathcal P_k=4\lambda T_{0k}.
\tag{3.3B.1}
$$

This construction can inherit positivity from the null energy condition and
it is exactly chiral for a directed null beam. Those are properties of a
quadratic flux probe.

## Why it is not the carrier map

The M1 source channels instead densitize the affine shell readings

$$
M\pm\frac12p_k.
$$

Their sum is $2M$ and their difference is $p_k$. A quadratic null contraction
has a stress-dependent even part and twice the shell tilt. For a beam with
$p_x=M$, SI gives

$$
\mathcal J_x^+=\frac32\mathcal M,
\qquad
\mathcal J_x^-=\frac12\mathcal M,
$$

whereas the null contraction places all weight in one channel. Exact chirality
therefore diagnoses the wrong mathematical object: a flux-like quadratic
probe rather than an affine carrier reading.

Static calibration also exposes a current mismatch. Choosing $\lambda$ so
that ordinary resting content has the required scalar weight makes the odd
package four times the physical current in the conventions of Equation
(3.3B.1). Earlier drafts used a presumed spatial coefficient and frame-drag
closure to turn that mismatch into an empirical no-go. That argument is no
longer independent because the directional action/readout chain is unresolved.
The structural mismatch already settles the source question.

## Result

Null contractions remain useful comparison objects: they explain NEC
positivity and exact beam chirality. They are not the densitized M1 shell
readings, so they do not define the Chapter 3 source channels.
